name: ANSI/IEEE earth connection symbol
summary: IEEE-oriented ground symbol with three diminishing bars, used for a general connection to earth.
description: US-practice drawings show a connection to earth ground with a vertical lead ending in three horizontal bars of decreasing length. The publisher's IEEE miscellaneous preview lists an Earth/Ground form alongside functional and protective forms, which the existing ANSI pages for those concepts already cover.

This is an independently drawn explanation rather than the IEEE graphic. The general ground symbol does not say whether the connection is for safety or function; where the distinction matters, use the protective or functional form. Grounding electrode details belong on the grounding plan.
readingNotes: Check whether a protective or functional form should be used instead.
Find the grounding electrode system on the grounding plan.
drawingChecklist: Use the general symbol only where the purpose is clear.
Keep symbol usage consistent across the set.
distinction: The general ground symbol marks any earth connection; the ANSI protective earth form specifically marks a safety ground.
